pages.title: A reagent in the blade
text: Anointing works a reagent's power into a weapon so every hit carries it. It is done at the [Song Bench](song_bench), and the weapon keeps it for good, until you choose to replace it.

A weapon holds **one anointment at a time**. Anointing it again with a different reagent swaps the old power for the new; anointing it with the one it already has is refused, so you never waste reagents by accident.

pages.title: How to do it
text: 1. Stand a [Resonance Totem](six_voices) within reach of the bench, with Pulse in the lattice.
2. Keep your Reagent Pouch on the hotbar, with at least **4 empowered** reagents of the kind you want.
3. Put the weapon in the bench's **weapon slot**, next to the output.
4. Click that reagent in the list to select it, then press **Anoint**. It costs the 4 reagents and **32 Pulse**.
The weapon's tooltip shows its anointment and the reagent it came from.

pages.title: What can be anointed
text: Every Spiritgear weapon, from the Blade to the [newer family](spiritgear_weapons), plus vanilla **swords**, **axes**, the **trident** and the **mace**.
Pack makers can open it to more through the `tribalpower:anointable` item tag.

pages.title: The eleven anointments
text: - **Searing** (Ember): burns the target and adds fire to every blow.
- **Stormcall** (Bolt): a quarter of blows arc lightning into two nearby hostiles.
- **Frostbite** (Chill): slows and freezes the target.
- **Venom** (Venom): poisons the target.
- **Gale** (Gust): hurls the target back and up.
- **Rooting** (Root): a fifth of blows root the target in place.

pages.title: The eleven anointments, continued
text: - **Sundering** (Shove): blows bite harder the more armour the target wears.
- **Echo** (Weave): a quarter of blows strike a second time for half.
- **Sapping** (Weaken): weakens the target.
- **Bloodthirst** (Hound): life steal, 15% of every blow comes back as health.
- **Mending** (Quiet): the weapon repairs itself as it strikes.
Anointments only fire on your own melee blows, not arrows or spells. Every number is in the `anointing` section of the common config, so a pack may tune them.
